title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page written on the back of a seminar announcement; the faint typed text showing through is Helmstetter's Clifford-algebra abstract. It works out a presentation of the integral linear group GL2(Z), viewed as the extended mapping class group of the torus (or of M_{1,1} / M_{0,4}), from the symmetries of the square lattice. This is the 'Lego' of the two one-dimensional Teichmüller pieces.

(1) The square-lattice piece. Take generators σ1, σ2 (reflections) and σ (rotation of order 4), with relations σ1² = σ2² = (σ1σ2)² = 1, σ1σ2 = σ², and σ1σσ1 = σ2σσ2 = σ⁻¹. They generate D_σ ≅ D4, the dihedral group of order 8. This is the automorphism group of Z² with its square form, i.e. the stabiliser of the point i.

(2) Transvections. Two transvections ρ1, ρ2 satisfy σ_i ρ_j σ_i = ρ_j⁻¹ and σρ1σ⁻¹ = ρ2. Since σ² = −1 is central, it follows that σρ2σ⁻¹ = ρ1.

(3) An amalgam is proposed: D_σ *_{D_{σ1}} D_{ρ1}, the group generated by ρ1 and σ, amalgamated along a common dihedral subgroup.

(4) A boxed alternative presentation uses generators σ, σ1, ρ1 with σ⁴ = ρ1² = 1, σ1σσ1 = σ⁻¹, and ρ1 commuting with σ1 and with σ². Here ρ1 is an involution commuting with the Klein four-group {1, σ1, σ², σ2}. It is then noted that σ2 = σ1σ² commutes with σ1, and he begins to compute σ1σ2 and σ2(ρ1).

(5) Explicit realisation on Z² = ⟨e1, e2⟩:
- σ1 = diag(1, −1);
- σ2 = τ∞ = diag(−1, 1);
- σ = [[0, −1], [1, 0]], i.e. e1 ↦ e2, e2 ↦ −e1;
- ρ1: e1 ↦ e1, e2 ↦ e2 − e1, i.e. ξ0 = [[1, −1], [0, 1]], a Dehn twist.
The figure with two perpendicular diameters illustrates σ² = −1.

(6) A second figure shows a disc with 12 marked boundary points a_i, b_i, c_i (i = 0..3), two crossing pairs of lines, and a hexagon. This looks like a picture of the Farey-type cell decomposition / modular tessellation with its square (D4) and hexagonal (D6) symmetry points. The final line, σ(ξ0) = ρ(ξ0) = ξ1, records conjugation of one Dehn twist into the adjacent one.

The aim is the classical amalgam GL2(Z) ≅ D4 *_{D2} D6, or equivalently PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. Grothendieck is reconstructing it 'by hand' as part of his description of the Teichmüller groupoid in genus 0/1 with marked points.
errors: The transcription line 'e1 e2 = −e2' should read 'σ1 e2 = −e2'; the image and the matrix σ1 = diag(1, −1) confirm this.

Inconsistent use of ρ1. In the upper part, ρ1 satisfies σ1ρ1σ1 = ρ1⁻¹ and is realised as the infinite-order transvection [[1, −1], [0, 1]]. In the box, ρ1² = 1 and σ1(ρ1) = ρ1. The boxed ρ1 must be a different element (an involution), so the two attempts are not compatible as written.
The amalgam 'D_σ * D_{ρ1} over D_{σ1}' is left unverified. The computations σ1σ2 = … and σ2(ρ1) = … are left blank.
All the stated relations I checked hold for the given matrices: σ1σ2 = σ² = −I, σ1σσ1 = σ⁻¹, σ1ρ1σ1 = ρ1⁻¹, σρ1σ⁻¹ = [[1, 0], [1, 1]] = ρ2, and σ2 = σ1σ².

ideas.what: Dihedral group D4 generated by two commuting reflections and a quarter-turn, realised as the automorphisms of the square lattice Z²
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of i in GL2(Z) (D4 of order 8)

ideas.what: Presentation of GL2(Z) / modular group as an amalgam of finite dihedral groups, using transvections ρ1, ρ2 conjugated by σ
ideas.modern_name: GL2(Z) ≅ D4 *_{D2} D6; PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 (Serre, Trees)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller groupoid in genus 0/1 and the M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} building blocks, but not this explicit computation

ideas.what: Dehn twists ξ0, ξ1 as conjugate transvections, with a picture of the modular tessellation featuring square and hexagonal symmetry points
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of the torus; Farey tessellation; Teichmüller 'Lego' in genus one
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; Lego viewpoint: Grothendieck (Esquisse), later Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard scratch computations of the dihedral and transvection presentation of GL2(Z) / the torus mapping class group. They are classical and partly inconsistent and unfinished, and contain nothing beyond the known Lego picture of the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: 'D_σ * D_{ρ1}' with 'D_{σ1}' written underneath is probably the amalgamated product D_σ *_{D_{σ1}} D_{ρ1}.
'D_4' under D_σ records the identification D_σ ≅ D4.
'σ2 = σ1σ² a [?] σ1' likely reads 'σ2 = σ1σ² commute à σ1'; the next line is 'calculer σ1σ2 ='.
In 'ρ1 e2 = e2 − e1', the crossed-out text is a struck false start, not a term.
The last line reads 'σ(ξ0) = ρ(ξ0) = ξ1'.
τ2'' is identified with τ∞ (the '‖' below it means equality).
